selected_result: Componentwise data-perturbation condition bound for Lagrange interpolation

bibliographic_source.title: The Numerical Stability of Barycentric Lagrange Interpolation

paper_pdf.path_basename: P13_The numerical stability of barycentric Lagrange interpolation.pdf

paper_locations.anchor: Equation (2.1), Definition 2.1, Lemma 2.2, and the componentwise perturbation inequality following equation (2.2)

task_clarification: Fix n+1 distinct interpolation nodes x_0, ..., x_n and an evaluation point x. Let ell_j(x) be the Lagrange basis coefficients and p_f(x) = sum_(j=0)^n f_j*ell_j(x).
Assume p_f(x) is nonzero and define cond(x,n,f) = (sum_(j=0)^n |ell_j(x)*f_j|)/|p_f(x)|.
For a componentwise perturbation satisfying |Delta f_j| <= epsilon*|f_j| for every j, formalize the paper's bound |p_f(x)-p_(f+Delta f)(x)|/|p_f(x)| <= cond(x,n,f)*epsilon.
scope_constraints: Use exactly n+1 nodes and data values indexed from 0 through n.
The nodes are distinct and remain fixed; only the data values are perturbed, and epsilon is nonnegative.
The evaluation point remains fixed and the unperturbed interpolant value there is nonzero.
Retain the paper's Lagrange basis coefficients and its stated condition-number expression.
The selected result is the perturbation inequality; exact attainment and the separate lower bound cond(x,n,f) >= 1 are outside its required conclusion.
Do not reinterpret this result as an algorithmic floating-point evaluation guarantee.
